name: splint
why: Secure programming lint from the 1990s C security era; an old-school static analyser worth a historical poke.

brief.what_it_is: Splint is a tool for statically checking C programs for security vulnerabilities and coding mistakes. Its homepage describes it as annotation-assisted lightweight static checking, and says that with minimal effort it works as a better lint. Adding annotations to the source lets it perform stronger checks than any standard lint can. You feed it C source files and it reports likely problems. The homepage does not describe the output format.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as Secure Programming Lint, and also as SPecifications Lint and First Aid for Programmers. The stated aim is to catch security holes and coding mistakes in C with a lightweight tool that programmers can extend with annotations.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says the tool statically checks C source. Programmers can add annotations to their code, and the tool uses them to do deeper checking than plain lint. The README and homepage give no further detail on the analysis itself. The cited papers cover buffer overflow detection and dynamic memory error detection.
brief.install_notes: The homepage lists version 3.1.2 with a source download on GitHub and a historical tgz distribution. A Windows installer was made by a third party, Mao Yu, at github.com/maoserr/splint_win32, and the news page dates it to 5 August 2010. Older news items mention an OS/2 binary from Herbert Martin Dietze and a Borland C++Builder (free compiler) build, with directions in a bcc32.html page. A Splint GUI by Christoph Thielecke was also published in 2008. The homepage does not mention runtimes, accounts, or configuration.
brief.standout: It is an early annotation-driven checker for C. The programmer can start with plain lint-style checking and add annotations for stronger checks, which is a different trade-off from the usual lint tools that work without annotations.
brief.status: Quiet. The newest release on the homepage is 3.1.2, announced 12 July 2007. The newest news item is 5 August 2010, and it is about a third-party Windows installer. The FAQ was last updated 3 May 2004. The GitHub README is a single line pointing to splint.org. I did not see commit dates.
brief.caveats: The GitHub README is thin and sends readers to splint.org for documentation. I did not follow the Splint Manual link, because the homepage gave no URL for it. Several platform builds are historical, and the homepage points to third-party builds for Windows, OS/2, and Borland. I did not see a license on either page. The homepage says nothing about current C standards or compilers. The homepage gives a 2004 FAQ date and no date for the manual.
quotes: Splint is a tool for statically checking C programs for security vulnerabilities and coding mistakes.
With minimal effort, Splint can be used as a better lint.
If additional effort is invested adding annotations to programs, Splint can perform stronger checking than can be done by any standard lint.
